leagues.name: State-hosted UCI road races (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, China, Rwanda)
leagues.country: UAE / Saudi Arabia / Oman / China / Rwanda
notes: Event-host shape: these 7 races do not fit the schema yet (no event entity, no host/title-sponsor placement), so the races are recorded here as the entity list and every commercial fact is recorded in unsourced and as org deals, following the UFC, Esports World Cup and horse-racing precedents. clubs and kits arrays are empty.

The 7 races (2026): UAE Tour (UCI WorldTour, 16-22 Feb, won by Isaac del Toro), UAE Tour Women (Women's WorldTour, 5-8 Feb, won by Elisa Longo Borghini), AlUla Tour (UCI ProSeries 2.Pro, 27-31 Jan, won by Jan Christen), Tour of Oman (ProSeries, 7-11 Feb, won by Christian Scaroni), Muscat Classic (ProSeries one-day race, 6 Feb, won by Mauro Schmid), Tour of Guangxi (WorldTour season finale, 13-18 Oct), Tour du Rwanda (UCI Africa Tour 2.1, 22 Feb-1 Mar, won by Moritz Kretschy).

Separate the race owner/host (the state body) from the commercial operator: Abu Dhabi Sports Council owns the UAE Tour races with RCS Sport as organiser; the AlUla Tour site is run by ASO (c) with the Saudi Ministry of Sport and Royal Commission for AlUla as institutional partners; the Tour of Oman site is run by ASO (c) with the Omani Ministry of Culture, Sports and Youth organising; the Tour of Guangxi is organised by the People's Government of Guangxi and Wanda Group; the Tour du Rwanda is organised by the Rwanda Cycling Federation.

Muscat Classic and Tour of Oman overlap in 2026 reporting: Muscat Daily describes the 6 Feb Muscat Classic as opening the Tour of Oman programme, while Wikipedia lists it as a separate one-day race on the ProSeries calendar; the race's own site says it runs 'ahead of the Tour of Oman (7-11 February 2026)'. Both are counted here; the exact governance split is unresolved.

Not counted: the 2025 UCI Road World Championships in Kigali (21-28 Sept 2025, one-off host event, covered in claims and unsourced) and a possible 2026 Tour of Guangxi women's race, which was not verified.

Sponsorship is on race titles, presenting partnerships and leader's-jersey/stage sponsorship, not shirts; the UAE Tour's own sponsors page lists Presenting Sponsor (AD Ports Group), Jersey Sponsors, Stage Sponsors and stage partners. Host fees are not disclosed.

proposedRatings.reasoning: AD Ports Group is 'Established by Emiri Decree and owned by ADQ' (its own about-us page), and ADQ sits under the Government of Abu Dhabi in the existing owner chain - so the Presenting Partner of the state-owned UAE Tour is direct Abu Dhabi state money. Same UAE evidentiary base as the rated Etihad/Experience Abu Dhabi chain: the 2024 mass trial (43 life sentences rights groups called grossly unfair) upheld on appeal in March 2025. Serious, matching the existing chain rating; severe is reserved for live armed conflict.

Mubadala is the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund and a classification-jersey sponsor of the UAE Tour and UAE Tour Women. Same Abu Dhabi state record as the other rated UAE-chain sponsors (2024 mass trial, upheld 2025) -> serious. Note: the shared owners.json entry for mubadala has parentId null; the chain to the Government of Abu Dhabi should be set when this is merged (flagged in unsourced).

ADSC is the Emirate of Abu Dhabi's government sports authority (established 2006 by the UAE president, 'aligned to the emirate's leadership vision'), and it owns and organises both UAE Tour races - the state is not just a sponsor but the event's owner. Same UAE record (mass trial 2024, upheld 2025) -> serious, matching the Etihad/Experience Abu Dhabi chain rating.

AlUla is the destination brand of the Royal Commission for AlUla, a Saudi government agency (parentId government-of-saudi-arabia), and RCU co-organises the AlUla Tour with the Saudi Ministry of Sport - the race name itself is state branding. Same Saudi state record as the other rated Saudi sponsors (record 345 executions in 2024, Khashoggi assessment) -> serious; severe is reserved for armed-conflict-linked sponsors.
